findings: l.647 'By assumption, the quotient is Hausdorff': Hausdorffness of Gamma\M does not follow from the neighbourhood form of proper discontinuity alone (free wandering actions with non-Hausdorff quotients exist); it needs the separating form (IsProperlyDiscontinuous.separates, or local compactness with mathlib's definition). The structure itself needs neither Hausdorffness nor invariance of U.
questions: 'properly discontinuous' is not defined in the paper; reading taken: GX.IsProperlyDiscontinuous (nbhd meeting translates only through the stabiliser + distinct orbits separated); only its first half is used for the structure, and it is implied by the two standard definitions (proved).

findings: l.639 is false as written: a free, properly discontinuous action by homeomorphisms that are not (G,X)-morphisms admits NO structure on the quotient making the projection a (G,X)-morphism. Counterexample GX.gxQuotient_counterexample: Z/2 acting on the (translations of R)-manifold R ⊕ R by inl x ↦ inr 2x, inr x ↦ inl x/2 (free, properly discontinuous in the full reading IsProperlyDiscontinuous, continuous; ℝ ⊕ ℝ a (G,X)-manifold, all certified as conjuncts); no charted structure at all on the quotient makes the projection a (G,X)-morphism. Corrected form GX.gxQuotient adds 'by (G,X)-morphisms' (which prop:aeGXquotient does state).

hypotheses.paper: BTZ: u future lightlike, <v|u> < 0, x0 arbitrary
hypotheses.note: every x0, every future lightlike u (Q(u)=0, τ(u)>0), every v with <v|u> < 0 (GX.btz_whitehole_isom0): Isom_0 is transitive on (base point, future lightlike vector) (GX.exists_isom0_nullU), and P_θ is a parabolic one-parameter family in Isom_0 fixing x0+Ru pointwise (GX.parabConj, GX.parabConj_fix); the coordinate case u=(1,0,0) is GX.btz_whitehole / GX.btz_isom0

hypotheses.paper: variations: u spacelike, v spacelike or future/past timelike
hypotheses.note: coordinate reading u=(0,0,1) (the Isom_0-conjugation of an arbitrary spacelike u is not proved), P_θ the boosts fixing x0+Ru; the condition v_a v_b ≠ 0 is added: automatic for timelike v (GX.timelike_ab_ne_zero), necessary for spacelike v (GX.misnerDev_spacelike_counterexample)

findings: l.667 'Its singular locus is sing(M) = {r=0}' is false in general: GX.quotientBase_counterexample (alpha = 2π, X = C, G = translations, D(r,θ) = r e^{iθ}, every hypothesis of the example) has EMPTY singular locus while {r=0} is the apex. True: sing(M) ⊆ π{r=0} (GX.quotientBase_sing_subset).

l.664–667 dimension slip: cyl{n} := D_inf × R^n is (n+2)-dimensional and is said to have a local homeomorphism {r>0} → X ⊆ R^n and a quotient homeomorphic to R^n; read cyl{n} = D_inf × R^{n-2} (the Minkowski case uses (r,θ,z), z ∈ R, X = R^3), or the quotient as R^{n+2}. Formalized for D_inf × Z, with M ≅ C × Z (GX.cylHomeomorph).

l.673 (massive particle): with D(r,θ,z) = (z+σθ/α, r cos(θ/α), r sin(θ/α)) the deck generator θ ↦ θ+α of Γ_α acts by D ↦ (time translation by σ) ∘ (rotation of angle 1 radian), whatever α (GX.massiveDev_smul with c = 1/α: angle cα = 1). The cone angle is therefore 1 and the mass 1 − 1/2π, not the stated m = 1 − α/2π, unless α = 1. The stated mass needs D = (z+σθ/α, r cos θ, r sin θ) (c = 1, angle α). Both are formalized (GX.massive_particle for every angular speed c ≠ 0).

l.674–678 (extreme BTZ white hole): formalized in the paper's generality (GX.btz_whitehole_isom0: every x0, future lightlike u, <v|u> < 0, G = Isom_0); D is even a homeomorphism of {r>0} onto a half-space, holonomy P_α.

l.678 'Choosing D'(r,θ,t) = D(r,θ,−t) gives an extreme BTZ blackhole instead': D' = D ∘ T with T(r,θ,t) = (r,θ,−t) a Γ_α-equivariant homeomorphism of the cylinder, so T descends to an isomorphism of singular (G,X)-manifolds between the 'black hole' M' and the white hole M (GX.btz_blackhole_iso_whitehole, GX.btz_blackhole_isom0). As printed, the black hole is the white hole. A genuine black hole should reverse the time orientation of X (e.g. u past lightlike, or D composed with a time reversal of Minkowski space, which is not in Isom_0).

l.679 (Misner/BTZ variations, u spacelike): 'v spacelike' does not suffice: for u = (0,0,1) and the spacelike v = (1,0,1) (null coordinates, Q(v) = 1) the image of D lies in a plane, so D is not a local homeomorphism (GX.misnerDev_spacelike_counterexample). Needed: v not in the plane spanned by u and one null eigendirection of the boosts (v_a v_b ≠ 0), automatic for timelike v. Formalized with that condition (GX.misner_btz, GX.misner_isom0).
SCOPE: tachyons and photons (l.682–683, no formula in the paper) and the polyhedral gluings are not formalized; the variations are formalized for the coordinate spacelike u only.
questions: The later counterexample (l.1181) uses '𝔻' and 'the quotient map q : D_inf → 𝔻' without defining 𝔻 in ex:quotient_base; read as 𝔻 = Γ_α\D_inf (GX.Disc α, GX.discQuot α, homeomorphic to C by GX.discHomeomorph), presumably α = 1 since Y_0 = {θ ∈ ]0,1[}.
ex:quotient_base l.673: which developing map is intended for the massive particle of mass 1 − α/2π — (r cos θ, r sin θ), giving angle α, or the printed (r cos(θ/α), r sin(θ/α)), giving angle 1?
l.678: was the extreme BTZ black hole meant to use a past lightlike u (or a time reversal of X) rather than t ↦ −t on the cylinder, which yields a structure isomorphic to the white hole?
l.679: should the Misner/BTZ variations require v outside the span of u and a null eigenvector of the boosts (v_a v_b ≠ 0 in null coordinates)? 'v spacelike' alone allows a degenerate D.

labels.label: ex:conical

hypotheses.note: 0 < α; R^{n-2} read as any locally connected T2 nonempty Z

any rigid (G, C × Z) containing the rotation ρ_α; the paper's G = Isom+(E^n) = GX.IsomPlus E instantiated for every α > 0 and every n (GX.conical_isomPlus); witness also G = SO(2), Z = {*} (conical_circle)

hypotheses.paper: metric dz^2+dr^2+α r^2 dθ^2, θ ∈ R/Z
hypotheses.note: E^n_α = GX.ConicalSpace α E = C_α × E with the ℓ² metric, C_α the cone of angle α (the corrected angle); the printed metric (angle √α) is GX.conical_printed_metric and is refuted at α = 2π (GX.conical_printed_metric_two_pi)

findings: l.347: with θ ∈ R/Z the metric dz²+dr²+α r² dθ² has cone angle √α (a circle r = r0 has length √α·r0), not α. Lean witness: read as the cone C_{√α}, its apex is Euclidean iff α = 4π² and NOT Euclidean at the paper's α = 2π (GX.conical_printed_metric, GX.conical_printed_metric_two_pi), against 'cannot be extended … except for α = 2π'. The rest of the example (holonomy = rotation of angle α) and ex:consider_identifying need angle α, i.e. α² r² dθ² on R/Z (or r² dθ² on R/αZ). The corrected object is built: E^n_α = C_α × R^{n-2} (GX.ConicalSpace, ℓ²), C_α ported from lean-causal, proper and geodesic, C_2π ≅ ℂ, apex not Euclidean for α ≠ 2π; its metric topology is the quotient topology of Γ_1\(D_inf × R^{n-2}) (GX.conicalMetricHomeo) and it is Euclidean along the developing map on {r>0} (GX.conical_locally_euclidean_prod).

l.350–351: the holonomy is offered by the paper only as 'an obstruction', and it is one only for α ∉ 2πN*: for α ∈ 2πN*, α ≠ 2π, the holonomy is trivial and does not obstruct, so the argument as written does not cover those angles. The claim itself is true there as well (the developing map is k-to-1 around the axis, so no chart covers it): GX.conical proves support = univ ↔ α = 2π, and the whole axis singular for α ≠ 2π. The metric side agrees: Cone.apex_not_euclidean for every α ≠ 2π (GX.conical_metric).
questions: 'This geometrical structure cannot be extended to the whole R^n' read as: the maximal a.e. atlas of E_α = Γ_1\(D_inf × Z) does not cover the axis. The metric is the cone distance formula with the corrected angle α (ℓ²-product with R^{n-2}), not the Riemannian length metric (the library has no Riemannian metric); 'the printed metric has angle √α' is read through the length of the circle r = r0, i.e. as C_{√α}.

labels.label: ex:consider_identifying_point_wise_stabilizer

hypotheses.note: E^n = ℂ × E, E finite-dimensional Euclidean (R^{n-2}); Isom+ read as GX.IsomPlus E (affine maps whose linear part preserves |w|^2+|z|^2 with det > 0; Mazur–Ulam); rigid by IsRigidAction.subgroup of the affine group. The general theorem quotient_rotations also holds for any rigid G

hypotheses.paper: Γ ⊂ Stab(S) finite of order p
hypotheses.note: every subgroup of order p of the point-wise stabilizer Stab(S) ≅ SO(2) is μ_p (GX.ptStab_subgroup_eq_rootsOfUnity), so Γ = μ_p is no loss of generality

findings: l.635 'as a metric space Γ\M ≅ E^n_{2π/p}' holds only with the corrected cone angle of ex:conical (angle α, not the printed √α); proved for every n with that reading.
questions: 'The metric on reg(Γ\M) extends continuously to Γ\M' is read as: the quotient distance min_γ |γx − y| of μ_p\E^n is carried by a homeomorphism (GX.rotationsMetricHomeo, for the quotient topology) to the metric of E^n_{2π/p} = C_{2π/p} × R^{n-2} (GX.rotations_metric, every n), hence a metric on the whole quotient inducing its topology; the singular (G,X)-isomorphism μ_p\E^n ≅ E^n_{2π/p} is that isometry (GX.conical_quotient_rotations_isometry). With the printed metric of ex:conical the angle would be √(2π/p) and the claim false. The variations (H^n, S^n, KP^n) are not formalized.

hypotheses.note: for Z a real normed space (R^{n-2}): {r>0} ≅ ℂ × Z contractible, the projection a covering over π{r>0}, which is semilocally simply connected, and the covering is isomorphic over it to UniversalCover (GX.Topology.UniversalCover)

findings: l.685 'branched over its singular locus': the branching locus of D_inf × Z → M is π{r=0}, which can strictly contain sing(M) (GX.quotientBase_counterexample: α = 2π, sing(M) = ∅ while the cover branches at the apex).
questions: Read as: the cylinder is a covering over π{r>0}, branched over π{r=0} ⊇ sing(M), it is the universal covering of π{r>0}, and D induces a (G,X)-morphism on {r>0}; ex:consider_identifying is the α = 2π/p case of ex:conical (conical_quotient_rotations). Fox-universality (§3) is not formalized here.

extra_decls: GX.locallyConnectedSpace_prod (instance: products of locally connected spaces)
kb_proposals: Quotients: build the structure on Γ\M by pushAtlas (charts φ of N with φ∘π locally an element of G against the charts upstairs) + HasDecks; uniqueness on the TARGET (eq_of_isMaximalAEAtlas_right) only needs π open surjective; isCoveringMapOn_of_smul_disjoint (Covering/Quotient.lean) gives the local homeomorphism on the free locus with no local compactness.

A space defined by a generated topology (𝔻_∞): prove the neighbourhood basis at the special point by induction on GenerateOpen, an open embedding for the regular part, then continuity_of_posEmb-style criteria; mathlib has no LocallyConnectedSpace instance for products at this pin (GX.locallyConnectedSpace_prod).
IsLocalHomeomorphOn f s requires f = e GLOBALLY as functions; use IsLocalHomeomorphOn.mk (EqOn on the source) and a congr lemma (GX.IsLocalHomeomorphOn.congr_of_eqOn) when changing the map off s.
PUnit is universe-polymorphic: in a theorem quantifying over atlases on X × PUnit, universe metavariables split; use Unit.

Local homeomorphism on an open set from one on the subtype: IsLocalHomeomorphOn.of_comp_right with Subtype.val (GX.isLocalHomeomorphOn_of_subtype); factor developing maps through cylPosHomeo (log-polar coordinates, {r>0} ≅ ℂ × Z).

Rigidity of affine groups: AffineMap.ext_on + IsOpen.affineSpan_eq_top; subgroups inherit IsRigidAction (GX.IsRigidAction.subgroup). Isom_0 of a Lorentzian form as a Subgroup of V ≃ᵃ[ℝ] V: time orientation as 'maps the future cone into itself' makes closure under inverse a 3-line argument.

IsRegularOn.of_exists needs ONE chart pair per point: an isomorphism of quotient structures is proved by composing the local chart equations of the two projections (regLocusOf_eq) and pushing along the projection's local homeomorphism (conical_quotient_rotations).
The cone C_α of lean-causal ports into GX unchanged; only its GeodesicSpace instance (Causal.Static) must become a theorem.
A developing map composed with a fixed element of G pulls back the same atlas (GX.devAtlas_smul): transporting a quotient structure by an element of Isom_0 is a rewrite, not a new proof.

A Γ-equivariant homeomorphism T of the cover with D' = D ∘ T descends (GX.orbitsHomeomorph) to an isomorphism of the two quotient structures (GX.isAEMorphismOf_quotientBase): check for it before calling two examples different.
